These are the refusals whose **outcome** differs in the clone: a guard the clone lacks (the original drops the order, the clone carries it out), or a different test order (a different line when two refusals hold). Wording alone is #801; R36, R37 and R41 (Rename and Split unit) are on #721; disbanding a regular unit away from a city is #713.

| Row | The original refuses | Play | The clone |

| R38 | Split unit with two or more units selected: *"You can only split 1 unit at a time."* | CU03 | `godot/UI/Dialogs/ChangeUnitsDialog.cs` acts on the first selected unit (as it does for Rename, R36 on #721) |

| R47 | Recruit unit at 100 % mobilisation: *"Your mobilisation rate is already 100%."* | RC02 | no refusal; `RecruitStandingUnitCommandHandler.cs:24–29` records it as `[open]` and only clamps the rate |
| R30 | Transfer into an army aboard a fleet whose ships are fewer than `troops / 500` after the move: *"This fleet can not carry any more troops."* (the unit stays) | TR3b | `ArmyTransferCommandHandler.cs` has no fleet-capacity test |
| P08 | Change units → Disband asks *"Are you sure you want to disband N unit."* (`units` when N > 1) and acts on every selected unit | CU07, CU08 | `ChangeUnitsDialog.DisbandSelected` (`:212`) asks nothing and disbands the first selected unit only |

## Different test order (the first failing test is the only box)

| Function | The original's order | Play | The clone's order |
|---|---|---|---|
| Join fleets | R15 (over 100 ships) before R16 (one carries an army) | **UF05c**: both hold, the 100-ship line appears | army first (`src/IC2.Engine/Naval/Commands/JoinFleetsCommandHandler.cs:79` before `:88`) |
| Repair fleet | R13 (no own city near) before R14 (carrying an army) | — | army first (`RepairFleetCommandHandler.cs:46` before `:77`) |
| Split fleet | R17 (under 20 ships) before R18 (carrying an army) | — | army first (`SplitFleetCommandHandler.cs:42` before `:50`) |
| Fortify | R22 (under siege), R23 (at 100), R24 (pending) | — | 100, pending, siege (`src/IC2.Engine/Cities/Orders/OrderCityCommandHandler.cs:59`, `:67`, `:75`) |
| Recruit mercenaries | before the dialog opens: R08 (20 units), R09 (100,000 troops), R10 (enemy city), R11 (supplies), R12 (fleet); then per hire R25 (purse), R26, R27 | — | one command: R25 (`HireMercenaryCommandHandler.cs:117`), R26 (`:125`), R08 (`:135`), R10 (`:151`), R11 (`:167`), R27 (`:178`); so a short purse is reported before low supplies or an enemy city. T113's entry already states the original's order for its dialog |

## A count

The Split army dialog counts **the nation's** armies against the 198 cap (`godot/UI/Dialogs/ArmyDialogModels.cs:353`, `:374`); the original's cap counts every army in play (`DAT_004a0324 < 0xc6`, report row R01's note and "Orders that fail without a box"), as the engine does (`SplitArmyCommandHandler.cs:69`). The engine still refuses, so only the dialog's own refusal is reached wrongly.

## Derived only (the report's unaudited columns; listed so triage can weigh them, not as confirmed)

- **Army-to-army transfer clamps per unit** (R28–R33): each selected unit is tested, last slot first; a failing unit stays and the others still move; the boxes follow the loop. The clone rejects the whole transfer (`ArmyTransferCommandHandler.cs:125`, `:134`).
- **R12**: Recruit mercenaries for an army aboard a fleet already short of space refuses before the dialog (*"Your fleet cannot carry any more troops."*); not played.
- **Disband army aboard a fleet**: the original's `TUnitMap_DisbandArmy` tests only the own city near the army (R05); the clone also refuses an army aboard (`DisbandArmyCommandHandler.cs:35`). Whether the original disbands an army aboard a fleet next to its city was not played.
- **R48**: Recruit unit at a non-capital city whose fortification is 74 or less (*"This city's fortification has fallen below 75%."*); which cities may recruit is #515.

To triage under build-process §4.8. The clone is more permissive than the original in every missing-guard row.

Found by T147's implementer (PR #797, session ses_eef69ab3dffercZjL9J46sIdq2) and reproduced on unchanged origin/main (433efe6) before any T147 change.

**What is wrong.** `godot/Checks/SidePanelToggleCheck.cs`'s `ShowsArmyView()` decides that the context panel shows an army by finding a `Disband` button in it. T111 (PR #734, 3de8269) deliberately moved the army orders, Disband included, out of `ContextPanel`'s army panel into their own dialogs, so the check now fails three assertions on main: *the panel shows the army view*, *the panel's army view survived hide and show*, *the shown panel is the army view of the army selected while hidden*. The check scene is not run in CI (fix #694 wires the unwired check scenes), so it went unnoticed.

**Reproduction.** `godot --headless --path godot res://Checks/SidePanelToggleCheck.tscn --quit-after 600` on main: exit 1, those three FAIL lines.

**Fix (the fix lane, build-process.md §4.10).** In `godot/Checks/SidePanelToggleCheck.cs` only: identify the army view by something the army panel still shows (its army name or troop line, or a ContextPanel accessor that already exists), not by the Disband button. No change to ContextPanel or any rule. DoD: the check exits 0 with 0 FAIL on main after the change, and its three assertions fail if ContextPanel is made to show a city view instead (a mutation, uncommitted); `dotnet build godot/IC2.MapViewer.csproj` green.

**Triage (main session, 2026-10-06):** a fix (it stays in the file it names and changes no rule's outcome), in the v0.5.0 gate because it blocks T147's Done-when 5.

**What the clone does.** A human army's move that ends next to a non-hostile city runs automatic resupply: `GameSession.ApplyAutomaticResupplyIfAgainstANonHostileCity` (`src/IC2.Engine/Presentation/GameSession.cs` ~:1272-1305, T23's Done-when 2) calls `AutomaticResupply.ForArmy`, which fills supplies and, at an own city, sweeps a purse above 1,000 to the treasury or grants +500 from it to a purse under 500. `docs/game-design.md:103` and `docs/design-audit.md:264` state the same trigger (corrected on the evidence branch `evidence/oct05-batch`).

**What the original does** ([`2026-10-05-army-purse-writes-and-the-1000-cap.md`](https://github.com/diegoami/imperial-conquest-2-research/blob/9ae8924/docs/reports/2026-10-05-army-purse-writes-and-the-1000-cap.md), research `9ae8924`, "Reachability of row 10"; provisional):
- `FUN_0044F6D8` (the resupply) has two callers: the AI's per-army pass `FUN_0044E41C`, and the tail of the walk `FUN_0044D734` **only when the walk's target tile holds a city marker**. A human click on a terrain tile goes `CheckForMove` → `MoveHumanArmy` → `FUN_0044D734` with that terrain tile as target, and a click on a city marker goes to `SelectUnit` (attack or select). So **a human army never reaches the resupply** **[derived: code]**.
- **Observed** **[Wine candidate]**: army 0 ended its move at (100,42), next to Rome and Caere, both with stock: purse 100 → 100, supplies 170 → 170, treasury unchanged (`Q1_00_start.SAV` → `Q1_01_army0_at_100_42.SAV`). A click on an adjacent own city changed nothing either (`Q1c_00` → `Q1c_01`).
- The report notes that the feature inventory's row E12 describes the AI path and should be re-tagged for humans.

The AI trigger (`AiResupplyPass`) is the original's and is not part of this bug. Whether `improved` keeps a human resupply as a designed convenience is for triage, not decided here.

**What the clone does.** `HireMercenaryCommandHandler` refuses when `army.Money < cost` and then **deducts the cost**: `Money = army.Money - cost` (`src/IC2.Engine/Recruitment/Commands/HireMercenaryCommandHandler.cs:43`, `:90`); `MercenaryHired` carries the cost.

**What the original does** ([`2026-10-05-mercenary-hire-price-is-a-gate-not-a-charge.md`](https://github.com/diegoami/imperial-conquest-2-research/blob/9ae8924/docs/reports/2026-10-05-mercenary-hire-price-is-a-gate-not-a-charge.md), research `9ae8924`, provisional):
- **The price is a gate, not a charge.** `TRecruitMercs_RecruitMercUnit` @ 00441360 refuses when `purse < (troops × price[type] div 1000) × quality` ("Your army has too little money to pay these mercenaries.", :43633-43639); **nothing in the function writes the purse or the treasury** (:43618-43701). **[derived: code]**
- **Observed** **[Wine candidate]**: two hires (Samnite LI 3,868 q8, gate 24; Etruscan HC 960 q9, gate 27) left army 1's purse at 30 and the treasury at 2,270 both times (`Q4_03` → `Q4_04` → `Q4_06`, release `run-exp-v050-rules`); a purse of 20 was refused at the gate of 24.
- The first real charge is the quarterly pay, `((troops div 200) × price × quality) div 5` per unit, from the purse.
- `MercenaryHireCost.Compute`'s gate formula already matches (`(troops × price) / 1000 × quality`); only the deduction is wrong.

**Note for triage.** The handler is in T76's area (#330, in progress on another machine), which reworks the player's hire rule; whether this goes into T76 or runs as a fix after it is the main session's call. The original's order-level refusals (20 units, over 100,000 troops, an enemy city, supplies under 15 per 10,000 troops, the fleet's carry check) are already in T76's scope and are not part of this bug.

## What is wrong

`GameSession.PeaceTreatyOfferDialogText` (`src/IC2.Engine/Presentation/GameSession.cs` ~:387–390) prints the post-battle offer as:

- `After losing to you in battle, <Loser> are willing to end the war.` (human winner)
- `After defeating you in battle, <Winner> are willing to end the war.` (human loser)

Its own remarks mark the words after "willing to end" as **[designed]**: the decompile's report quoted only the prefix, and the comma and "the war." were filled in.

## The evidence

[`2026-10-05-battle-peace-offer.md`](https://github.com/diegoami/imperial-conquest-2-research/blob/main/docs/reports/2026-10-05-battle-peace-offer.md) (research `9e3eff0`, "For the clone: the facts to copy", item 1) read the box's painted text from the screenshots of the original. It is provisional and was seen only under Wine, so it is a **Wine candidate**:

- after a human defeat: "After defeating you in battle <Winner> are willing to end their war with you, if you agree to the terms below."
- after a human win: "After losing to you in battle <Loser> are willing to end their war with you, if you agree to the terms below."

The box goes on with "An honourable peace with no reparations or penalt[ies]" (clipped by the box), empty reparation lines, "If the peace terms are acceptable click YES." and "Otherwise to continue the war click NO."

So the merged sentence has a comma after "battle" that the original lacks, and it ends "the war." where the original has "their war with you, if you agree to the terms below.".

## Decided scope (the user's decisions of 2026-10-05)

- **This fix runs before T139** (#727), which displays its result. T139's window shows the original's whole "Offer of peace" box text, and that text comes from the engine, so this fix is where the engine's offer text becomes the original's whole box text; T139 types no text and changes none.
- **The engine's offer becomes the box's lines**, quoted from the report (Wine candidate), in this order:
  1. the offer sentence: "After defeating you in battle <Winner> are willing to end their war with you, if you agree to the terms below." when the human lost, or "After losing to you in battle <Loser> are willing to end their war with you, if you agree to the terms below." when the human won (no comma after "battle");
  2. "An honourable peace with no reparations or penalt[ies]" (the report reads it clipped by the box; the clone shows the full word "penalties", the user's decision of 2026-10-05);
  3. "If the peace terms are acceptable click YES.";
  4. "Otherwise to continue the war click NO.".
  The reparation lines, always empty in the original, are not lines the engine supplies. The box's title, "Offer of peace", is T139's window title.
- **Exposed as lines**: `PeaceTreatyOfferDialogText` (`GameSession.cs` ~:387), or the member this fix renames it to, returns the box's lines as an ordered list, so the CLI prints them (each on its own line, where it prints the one sentence today, ~:338) and T139 can read them as typed data and display them unchanged. Name the member in the PR, since T139 consumes it.
- **Expected changes**: the CLI output changes wherever an offer is raised, so the CLI goldens and tests that hold the line (`PeaceTreatyOfferTests` among them) change in this fix's own PR; that is expected, not a regression. The remarks' **[designed]** completion is replaced by the report's text.
- **Unchanged**: the engine's gate, its Yes (relation -18 both ways and the honourable news line) and its No (nothing written) match the report. Only the wording and the number of lines change.
- **The clip (decided).** The report reads the terms line as "penalt[ies]", clipped by the original's box. The user decided on 2026-10-05 that the clone does not reproduce the clip: the line ends "penalties" (design-audit.md §1.7 quotes `TBattlePols`'s line as "An honourable peace with no reparations or penalties").

Found by the stage-2 evaluation of the report (branch `evidence/peace-offer`).

Found by the stage-2 evaluation of the research report [`2026-10-05-information-window-fields-and-bands.md`](https://github.com/diegoami/imperial-conquest-2-research/blob/main/docs/reports/2026-10-05-information-window-fields-and-bands.md) (research `929c4d1`). The report is **provisional**: its code readings are from the decompile, and what it observed was seen under Wine only. Comment and provenance text only; no rule's outcome changes.

## 1. The morale tiers: six, not five

The army panel's morale word is `table[(m − 51) sar 2]` (`m − 48` below 51) read from the unity/loyalty word table's entry 4, and that table has six words: 40–54 *very low*, 55–58 *low*, 59–62 *normal*, 63–66 *high*, 67–70 *very high*, **71–74 *excellent***, 75 and above nothing (section "Morale"; every edge from 54/55 to 74/75 staged both sides). Saves hold 51–73. So 51…70 is the supply rule's clamp, not "exactly five 4-wide tiers" nor the field's bound. Text that says otherwise:

- `src/IC2.Engine/Model/Ruleset.cs:482–483`: *"The hard floor, 51 — also the base of the army panel's five 4-wide morale tiers"*.
- The `moraleFloor` provenance string in `data/rulesets/classical-faithful.json:275`, `data/rulesets/improved.json:277` and `data/rulesets/toy-ruleset.json:251`: *"the real bound of the field … 51...70 being exactly five 4-wide tiers"*.

The repository's documents are corrected on branch `evidence/info-window` (`design-audit.md` §2.9a, `investigations/thracia-supply-morale.md`).

## 2. The fleet supply percent

## What is wrong

Three `IC2.Data` readers find the SAV's 55-byte trailer by counting back from the end of the file:

- `src/IC2.Data/SaveTurnState.cs:65` — `var start = data.Length - 55;`
- `src/IC2.Data/SaveNewsLog.cs:82` — `var trailerStart = data.Length - 55;` (and the layout check that the news slots end exactly there)
- `src/IC2.Data/SavePendingOffer.cs:61` — `var offset = data.Length - 23;` (trailer `+32`)

That holds only when the battle flag (trailer `+54`) is 0. An original save written **during a tactical battle** has the flag set to 1 and carries the 2,105-byte battle block **after** the trailer (9 header bytes, 40 slots of 44, the 14 × 12 icon grid). On such a file the trailer starts at `length − 55 − 2,105`, so:

- `SaveTurnState` reads the end of the icon grid as the turn order and throws a misleading "turn order names nation 50, outside 0..15"-style error;
- `SaveNewsLog` throws its "layout does not account for the file length" error;
- `SavePendingOffer` does not throw: it silently returns two words of the icon grid as the pending offer.

So `OriginalSaveImporter` rejects a valid original save (or, for a caller of `SavePendingOffer` alone, misreads it).

## Evidence

- Research `dee8150`, [`2026-10-04-battle-probe.md`](https://github.com/diegoami/imperial-conquest-2-research/blob/main/docs/reports/2026-10-04-battle-probe.md) item 2: File → Save As inside a battle writes 134,254 bytes = 132,149 + 2,105, "block 12 present, flag 1"; the post-battle save of the same game is 132,149 bytes with flag 0. **[Wine candidate]**
- Same report, review notes: all 585 saves with a battle block in the probe and sweep releases are 134,254 bytes, the base 132,149 plus the 2,105-byte block, read with the research repository's `scripts/battle-block-check.py` from the layout of [`2026-10-04-decompiled-tactical-battle-rules.md`](https://github.com/diegoami/imperial-conquest-2-research/blob/main/docs/reports/2026-10-04-decompiled-tactical-battle-rules.md) §1 (**[confirmed: code, static]** for the layout).
- [`decompiled-sav-file-layout.md`](https://github.com/diegoami/imperial-conquest-2-research/blob/main/docs/reports/decompiled-sav-file-layout.md) (corrected in research `b5db496`): the battle block is written after the battle flag.
- `SaveTurnState`'s own doc comment (~:9–15) describes the trailer as "the 55-byte trailer of known SAV files", checked on 54 saves, none of them written in a battle.

## Why it matters now

T129 (the tactical golden master) imports mid-battle saves: its resumed series "starts from the imported block" of `gate2_a_BATTLE05.SAV`, and its `OriginalBattleBlockImport` takes "a `SaveBattleBlock` and its imported `GameState`". T129's Owns include only `SaveTurnState.cs` (parsing the flag and exposing the block), not `SaveNewsLog.cs` or `SavePendingOffer.cs`, so as planned it cannot import such a save.

## Suggested shape (not decided)

Locate the trailer once — the first `length − 55` whose flag byte is 0, or `length − 55 − 2,105` when the byte at `length − 2,105 − 1` is 1 — in one shared helper, and use it in all three readers. Whether this runs as a `fix` before T129 or is folded into T129's Owns is for triage.

Found by `/process-evidence` stage 2 on research `dee8150`.

`CoastalCity.IsCoastal` (`src/IC2.Engine/Naval/CoastalCity.cs:33`) calls a city coastal when any of its eight neighbours is a tile with `passableByFleets` (codes 0 and 1). `OrderFleetCommandHandler` (`src/IC2.Engine/Naval/Commands/OrderFleetCommandHandler.cs:36`) refuses only a city that fails that test.

Applied to `data/worlds/classical-mediterranean.json` and its terrain sidecar, this test gives exactly the report's coastal counts for all 16 nations: Dacia 0, Galatia 0, **Media 2**. Media's two are **Derbend (303,12)** and **Ardabil (309,37)**, both on a closed body of 617 water cells (the Caspian), not connected to the 10,908-cell Mediterranean body. So `order-fleet derbend …` by Media is accepted where the original refuses Media outright.

## Why it matters

The clone lets Media build a fleet, which the original (under Wine) does not. A Media fleet could not reach the Mediterranean anyway, but it costs `ships × 10` and upkeep, and the AI or a player could order one.

## Open before a fix

The original's test is not known. "Not on a closed sea" and "next to sea code 0 that connects to the main sea" both fit the three refusals; a lead from this evaluation: each of the 13 ports the game named is the nation's coastal city (by the clone's test) nearest its capital, 13 of 13, so the game appears to pick the port itself. A code read of `TPremierForm_BuildNewFleet` (`0x0045B3A8`) for its coastal test settles both. T109's Build fleet dialog (status:blocked) consumes this refusal.

The OpenCode reviewer is told to type its worktree's path on every git command. A mistyped path ends the review.

**Where:**
- `.opencode/agents/external-reviewer.md:26-27`: "Pass `git -C <worktree>` explicitly on every git command".
- `scripts/external-review.ps1:519` (the OUTPUT RULES the script appends to the prompt): "The worktree you are in is $worktree at $headSha. Pass git -C "$worktree" explicitly."

**The failure it invites** (seen in a sibling repository, harness_imperial#15, 2026-10-02): in its first real review, the reviewer model's first command was `git -C "<worktree>" rev-parse HEAD && git -C "<worktree>" …`. In the second `-C` it mistyped a 90-character path (one extra character in a UUID). OpenCode auto-rejected the path as `external_directory`, which ends `opencode run`, and the review was lost after 17 s. Our review worktrees are `C:\Users\diego\projects\ic2-work\<pr>-external-review-<8 hex>`, about 60 characters with a random suffix. The `-C` rule buys nothing for the OpenCode reviewer, because the script already starts OpenCode inside the worktree (`--dir` and the process's working directory).

**The fix (the OpenCode reviewer only):**
1. Both the agent file and the script's prompt say: your working directory is the worktree; run git there as it is, without `-C`, and never type the worktree's path. The mutation restore step is `git checkout -- <file>`, run in the worktree.
2. A stronger tree proof. The first tool call prints `git rev-parse --show-toplevel`, `git rev-parse HEAD` and `git diff --name-only origin/main...HEAD`. The top level must be the worktree the prompt names (the script states it) and HEAD the commit it names ($headSha), and the diff must not be empty. Otherwise the reviewer says it is in the wrong tree and stops.
3. The deny rules: keep `git -C * push*`, `git -C * commit*`, `git -C * stash*` and `git -C * worktree *`, and **add** `git commit*`, `git stash*` and `git worktree *`. Today only `git push *` is denied without `-C`, so dropping `-C` would otherwise allow a plain commit, stash or worktree command.
4. A test in `external-review.ps1 -SelfTest`: the prompt the script builds, and the agent file's body (not its permission block), no longer ask for `git -C`; the prompt names the worktree and the head commit for the tree proof; and the agent file denies the plain commit, stash and worktree forms. Break each place by hand, watch the test fail, and restore it.
5. Afterwards, `grep -n "git -C"` over the agent file and the script's prompt text: only the deny rules may remain. (The script's own PowerShell calls such as `git -C $repo worktree add` are the script's, not the reviewer's, and stay.)

**Out of scope:**
- The implementer (`external-implement.ps1`, `external-implementer.md`) keeps `git -C`.
- `docs/build-process.md` Appendix B keeps `git -C`: it is the Claude Opus reviewer's template, and a Claude agent's shell returns to the main checkout on every call, so `-C` is what keeps it in its tree.

**Lesson:** the main session records it on the wiki's Process incidents page after the merge.

Files: `.opencode/agents/external-reviewer.md`, `scripts/external-review.ps1`.

**Defect.** `CityOrderProgressSystem` (`src/IC2.Engine/Cities/Orders/CityOrderProgressSystem.cs:89`) completes a fortification order that reaches 100% at **100**, in both presets. Its own remarks (`:9-23`) chose that reading over the literal transcription and marked it `[open]`, pending "order a fortification and save each turn until it completes". That check has now been made, and the original ends such an order at **0**.

**Evidence.**
- **Code, instruction by instruction:** the weekly tick `FUN_004514EC` at `0x4515A2`–`0x4515FA` does `word += min(10, word / 100)`, then `word -= min(1000, (word / 100) × 100)`, the second line reading the word **after** the addition. When the current level lands on exactly 100, `word / 100` counts one extra hundred and the whole word is removed (report §2).
- **Live, one headless turn under Wine** (report §3): Ariminum planted at 595 (95% + 5 pending) was at **0** after one turn; the two controls in the same turn behaved as the formula says (Altinum 2550 → 1560, Capua 1857 → 867). Saves `fort_probe_before.sav` / `fort_probe_after.sav` in the fixtures repository, `saves/fortification-probe/`, SHA-256 in the report.
- **Which orders are hit:** exactly those with `current + points = 100` and `points % 10 ≠ 0` (95 + 5 → 0; 62 + 38 → 72 → 82 → 92 → 0). 60 + 40 completes at 100. An order to 75% is never affected.

**Why it is a defect, not a question.** design-audit §3 Q8 is answered: `classical-faithful` reproduces the original's identified bugs and `improved` fixes them silently, and "any further bug found later joins the same table rather than opening a new question". The precedent is `flags.bugPolicySiegeRatioClamp` (T63). So `classical-faithful` should end such an order at 0, and `improved` keep completing it at 100.

**Confidence.** The arithmetic is read at instruction level; the live result is one turn under Wine. docs/evidence-pipeline.md asks for one desktop confirmation of a Wine-only result before it settles a rule, so the triage may want that confirmation (fortify a town at 95% by 5 points and look one turn later) before the faithful preset changes.

**Related.** T67 ([#304](https://github.com/diegoami/imperial_conquest_2/issues/304)) owns `src/IC2.Engine/Cities/Orders/**` and its Done-when 5 asks `cityOrders._provenance` to name the completion-at-100 reading; the review branch `evidence/recruit-cities` updates that line to name this bug. **What happens.** Since the reboot of 2026-10-01, every `scripts/external-implement.ps1` and `scripts/external-review.ps1` run on the desktop fails before OpenCode creates a session. It exits 3 ("OpenCode unavailable"). Even `opencode session list` fails:

```
Error: Unexpected error

no such column: project_id
```

**Cause.**
- The OpenCode desktop app bundles its own CLI, `%APPDATA%\ai.opencode.desktop\cli\2.0.18\opencode-cli.exe`. It shares the default data directory `~/.local/share/opencode/` with the npm CLI 1.18.33 that the scripts run.
- On start, the desktop app moved `opencode.db` to its 2.x schema. The 2.0.18 CLI reads the database; 1.18.33 can't.
- `PRAGMA quick_check` is ok, so the database isn't corrupt, just newer.
- npm publishes no 2.x (`latest` is 1.18.34).

**Fix (fix lane).** `scripts/Invoke-OpenCodeWatched.ps1` gives every OpenCode process it starts its own data directory, so the desktop app can never reach it again:
- Before the first `Start-Process`, set `$env:XDG_DATA_HOME` for this process. Use `$env:IC2_OPENCODE_DATA_HOME` if set, else `$HOME\.local\share\ic2-opencode-1x`. The child processes inherit it: the `run`, the `session list` polling and the `export`. That keeps all three on the same database.
- Create `<that dir>\opencode\` if missing.
- Copy `auth.json` from the default `$HOME\.local\share\opencode\auth.json` into it when the copy is missing or older than the source, so a re-authentication carries over. **Copy only; never read, print or log its content.**
- Log one line saying which data directory the run uses.
- Nothing else changes: `~/.config/opencode/opencode.json` and the repository's `.opencode/agents/` are still shared.

**Verified by hand.** With `XDG_DATA_HOME` set to a new directory and `auth.json` copied, 1.18.33 creates a fresh database, `opencode session list` exits 0, and `opencode auth list` shows the OpenCode Zen and OpenRouter credentials.

**Owns:** `scripts/Invoke-OpenCodeWatched.ps1`.
**DoD:**
- With the fix, one real `scripts/external-review.ps1` run against a small PR, or a dry run plus a manual `opencode session list` through the watcher's environment, creates a session.
- Without the fix, it fails as above.

Non-blocking findings from T54's review (PR #219, merged as `52bc42f`). Approved on all five gates. Four of the reviewer's findings were corrected before merge; these two remain.

## N1 — adjacency is implemented twice and can drift

`DisbandArmyCommandHandler.cs:76` **open-codes** the Chebyshev literal instead of calling `AttackLegality.AreAdjacent`.

Proved by the reviewer's mutation C: **widening `AreAdjacent` to `≤ 2` leaves both disband rows green.** So the two definitions of "adjacent" are free to diverge, and nothing notices.

This matters more than a normal duplication because T54's whole DoD 4 argument for *not* making the radius ruleset data was that **adjacency is one inherent geometric bound shared by attack, siege and disband** — a ruleset field *"would invite a value that makes disband and attack disagree"*. That reasoning is right, and the implementation currently allows exactly the divergence it argues against, just in code instead of data.

**Fix**: have disband call `AreAdjacent`. One line, and it makes the single-definition claim true.

## N2 — only the army gate has an adjacency boundary theory

`AttackArmyCommand` pins adjacency with a four-case boundary theory. The **siege** and **naval** `NotAdjacent` fixtures sit **4 tiles apart**, so they would pass at radius 1, 2 or 3 alike.

Mitigated today by the single shared `AreAdjacent` — the army theory pins the shared implementation. But that mitigation is exactly what N1 undermines: if a second definition appears, the untested gates stop being covered by the tested one.

**Fix**: move the siege and naval fixtures to distance 2, so each gate fails at its own boundary. Cheap, and it removes the dependence on a mitigation that is only true while N1 holds.

---

## Recorded from the review, not defects

Three judgements worth not reopening:

- **The DoD 5 two-command sequence is sound.** The original auto-declares war in one click, and T54 spells it as `DeclareWarCommand` then attack — because T16's merged diplomacy guard text-scans every file under `src/IC2.Engine/Battle/**`, which is where the commands live. The reviewer's framing: the ordering is preserved by something **stronger than call order** — the war gate makes an undeclared attack *impossible*, not merely late. Whether to rescope that guard is [#221](https://github.com/diegoami/imperial_conquest_2/issues/221).
- **`TurnPhase.Orders` is deliberately empty.** A system there would have to *decide* to attack, which is T22's judgement, and would make the engine the attacker. The reviewer confirmed the phase is empty **and functional** — five test systems register there and run.
- **Elimination flags a nation rather than deleting it**, which is why delete-then-dangle is safer here than feared. The reviewer hardened the probe with fleets, a carried army, a JSON round-trip and revalidate, relation-matrix rows and turn-order resolution — all passing.

## One consequence for the user, not a defect

T54's naval docking rule is `[confirmed]` (*"You cannot attack a fleet docked at its own city !"*) but its **radius is `[derived]`** — one tile, matching the confirmed supply-provider radius, because no report decompiles the distance.

As written that gives every fleet an **8-tile immunity ring around every city its nation owns**, and the gate does not require that city to be a port. Honestly tagged, and the only radius available — but a large surface resting on an inference.

[`attack-and-siege-are-adjacency-orders.md`](https://github.com/diegoami/imperial-conquest-2-research/blob/main/docs/reports/attack-and-siege-are-adjacency-orders.md) proposes a **30-second recording** that would settle this and the 8-way-versus-4-way adjacency metric together. Worth capturing on the next play-through.

Two structural findings from T54's implementation (PR #219), both outside its Owns list, both **needing a decision rather than a patch**.

## N1 — `Ruleset` names neither the archer unit type nor the fortification order

Three merged resolver entry points take these as **parameters**, so every caller must supply them:

- `InstantBattleResolver.ResolveField` / `ResolveSiege` / `ResolveNaval` take an `archerUnitTypeId`
- the siege path needs the fortification order's id

T54 had to introduce `BattleCommandRuleset.ArcherUnitTypeId = "archers"`, tagged `[designed]` **as a lookup** with a stated search: every `UnitTypeRules` field (`Shots`/`Range` belong to the tactical shell, and deriving "archer" from them would invent a rule), all of `Ruleset` for a pointer field, and the reports for a name in the data. The **id itself is well-sourced** — original type code 2 → `IC2.Data.UnitCatalog`, both shipped rulesets, and `ArmyNaming`'s canonical list — and a ruleset missing it gets a typed rejection rather than a throw.

For the fortification order it avoided a second literal entirely, finding the order **by behaviour** instead: `CityOrderRule.WipedBySiegeAttempt`, which is `FUN_0044B27C`'s own `if (fort > 100) fort = fort % 100`. That is the better pattern.

**The real fix is a `Ruleset` pointer field for each**, so the id lives in ruleset data like every other constant and callers stop threading it. Until then each new caller re-solves the same problem, and the `[designed]` tag propagates.

## N2 — T16's diplomacy guard now scans a directory it was not written for

`FieldBattleTests.AssertNoBattleSourceReferencesDiplomacy` text-scans **every** file under `src/IC2.Engine/Battle/**` for references to the Diplomacy namespace. It was written to protect **T16's resolver** — that the resolver *publishes* `PeaceTreatyTriggered` rather than calling diplomacy — and it predates `Battle/Commands/**` existing.

T54's commands live there now. So the guard also forbids an **attack command** from calling `RelationTransitions.DeclareWar`, even though the original does declare-war-and-attack in **one click**.

T54 proved the constraint rather than assuming it: a scratch file naming `RelationTransitions` fails `DoD08_PeaceTreatyTriggeredIsPublishedWhenTheRollAndBothGatesPass`. That test is outside T54's Owns, so it did not touch it, and instead spelled the confirmed sequence as **two commands in the confirmed order** — which `DeclareWarCommand`'s own merged remarks already document as the auto-declaration path.

**That is a defensible outcome, not a broken one.** But it is a constraint imposed by accident: the guard's blast radius grew when a new directory appeared under the path it scans.

**The decision**: either scope the scan to the resolver files it was written for (a narrow grant on `FieldBattleTests.cs`) and let the one-command form become possible, or keep the two-command form deliberately and **say so in T16's guard**, so the next implementer meets a stated rule rather than an unexplained failure.

## A related note, not a defect

T54's DoD 4 tests live under `tests/IC2.Engine.Tests/Battle/Commands/` although they exercise disband, because its Owns list granted no `tests/IC2.Engine.Tests/Armies/**` and — once DoD 3 removed any reason to touch movement — no movement-test home either. The implementer stated this in the file's own remarks and in the PR rather than leaving it to be inferred. Worth relocating whenever a task next owns the armies tests.

Found by T54's implementer. **This is a live defect in merged T18 code**, and it has a likely root cause worth acting on rather than patching around.

## The defect

**`CityState.UnderSiege` is written by no code anywhere in the engine.** Four references exist:

| | |
|---|---|
| the model field | `GameState.cs` |
| initialisation | `GameStateFactory.cs`, always `false` |
| T17's cascade gate | reads it — skips a city already contested |
| T18's fortify refusal **and** its `fort %= 100` wipe | read it |

So **T18's DoD line *"a siege attempt clears a pending fortification order"* is unreachable in production.** It has a passing test, because a test constructs a `CityState` with `UnderSiege = true` directly — which is legitimate as a fixture, and is what its brief told it to do. But nothing in a real game ever sets the flag.

Same class as [#215](https://github.com/diegoami/imperial_conquest_2/issues/215): a rule that is correct, tested, and cannot be reached.

## The likely root cause — worth more than the symptom

T54's implementer proposes that **the original has no stored siege flag at all**, and the evidence is good:

- The fortification tick is gated on **`FUN_004497cc`**, the `[confirmed]` *"hostile army adjacent"* predicate — **which this engine already implements**, as `Economy/HostileArmyAdjacent`.
- The wipe happens **at the siege attempt itself**, not from a persisted state.

If that holds, `UnderSiege` is a **field this reimplementation invented** to stand in for a predicate the original evaluates on demand. The fix is then not "find who should set the flag" but "replace the flag with the predicate" — and the flag itself should go.

That also explains why no task ever owned the producer: there is nothing to produce.

## Why nobody caught it

The reads were added by three different tasks, each correctly. T17 gated its cascade on it (reviewed twice). T18 refused orders on it and wiped on it (reviewed once). T54 found it only because it swept for production callers of the battle path and noticed the flag had none.

**Three correct consumers and no producer** is the same shape as #215's two correct decisions and one unreachable command.

## What a fix needs

1. **Settle whether the original stores a siege flag or evaluates a predicate.** `FUN_004497cc` is the lead. If it is a predicate, delete `CityState.UnderSiege` and route all three consumers through `HostileArmyAdjacent`.
2. If it *is* stored, find the producer and say which task owns it.
3. Either way, **T18's wipe and T17's cascade gate must end up exercised by a real game path**, not only by a hand-built fixture.

## Owner

Spans `Model/GameState.cs`, `Cities/Orders/**` (T18's), `Cities/Capture/**` (T17's) and possibly `Economy/**`. **No single existing task owns it** — this wants its own small task, and picking the owner matters more than the fix.

Note it is **not** blocking: nothing produces a wrong answer today, because the unreachable paths simply never run.

Reported by the user from the Godot map viewer: *"the Gaul army's color is the same as Rome's"*. Confirmed, and checking the palette turned up two further collisions that are **exact**.

`godot/MapViewer.cs:595-614`, `OwnerColor(ushort code)`. Sixteen nations, but only **fourteen distinct colours**:

| Pair | Codes | Colour | Status |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **Carthage / Media** | 1 and 14 | `(1, 0, 0)` pure red | **byte-identical** |
| **Ptolemaic / Illyria** | 3 and 9 | `(0, 0, 0.5)` navy | **byte-identical** |
| **Rome / Gaul** | 0 and 6 | `(0.5, 0, 0.5)` vs `(0.5, 0, 0)` | differ only in the blue channel |

The user's report is the third row: Rome and Gaul differ by one channel, and at army-marker size against the viewer's dark background (`Background = (0.07, 0.11, 0.15)`) dark purple and maroon read as the same colour. The first two rows are worse — those nations are genuinely **unpaintable apart**, whatever the size.

Nation codes verified against a real save's nation table (`11.sav`): 0 Rome, 1 Carthage, 2 Seleucid, 3 Ptolemaic, 4 Macedonia, 5 Numidia, 6 Gaul, 7 Greece, 8 Celtiberia, 9 Illyria, 10 Dacia, 11 Bithynia, 12 Galatia, 13 Armenia, 14 Media, 15 Thracia.

## Scope

Viewer-only. `src/IC2.Inspect` has **no** palette of its own — `--render-map` does not share this code — so nothing else is affected, and no decoded data is wrong. This is purely how the read-only research viewer paints owners.

## Fix

Sixteen distinguishable colours, checked against each other **and against the dark background** at the sizes actually drawn (city rect, army flag, fleet sail — the flag is the smallest and the one the user hit). Worth picking a palette designed for categorical separation rather than adjusting two entries and re-colliding somewhere else; the legend at `:52` should stay readable too.

Note `:178` special-cases codes `4, 5, 7, 8, 13, 14` to draw a dark glyph instead of a light one, i.e. those are the palette's "light" colours — any recolouring has to keep that list in step, or city glyphs go invisible.

## Ownership

`godot/**` is **T24**'s Owns list. T24 is the Godot main game screen and does not otherwise touch the inspector viewer, so this needs routing: either fold into T24, or into whichever task next opens `MapViewer.cs`. Not urgent — the viewer is a research tool, not the game UI — but it actively misleads while reading real saves, which is exactly what it is for.

Non-blocking findings from T45's review ([build-process.md §4.5](https://github.com/diegoami/imperial_conquest_2/blob/main/docs/build-process.md)). Task: T45 (#129), PR #142, squash-merged as `192093a`. **Nothing here blocks anything** — all five gates passed, and the reviewer ran five mutations (the three asked for, plus two of its own).

Review: https://github.com/diegoami/imperial_conquest_2/pull/142#issuecomment-5728975646

There is an irony worth stating: T45 exists to pin behaviour with tests, and these are defects in those tests. They are all in one file, so they fold cheaply into whichever task next touches `tests/IC2.Engine.Tests/Economy/**`.

---

## Open items

### N1 — the mid-week test's supply constant passes *through* a signed overflow

`tests/IC2.Engine.Tests/Economy/WeeklyMovesMaximumTests.cs:182`. `SupplyTons: 10_000_000` reaches `SupplyCapacity.PercentFull`, which computes `9_999_904 * 10_000 = 99,999,040,000` — past `int.MaxValue`. It wraps unchecked to `1,214,792,192`, giving pct ≈ 25,217, which lands in the regen branch, so the test passes.

It passes **because of** the wrap, not because "supply is set far above any plausible capacity" as the comment at lines 170–173 claims. That makes it brittle in a non-obvious way: roughly **+93,300 more tons** would make the wrap land negative, the starving branch would fire, and the test would fail by exactly one move with a baffling message.

**Fix**: use something like `100_000` tons — pct ≈ 20,758, same branch, no wrap — and correct the comment.

### N2 — the mid-week assertion is vacuous with respect to production code

Same file, `:204`. `midWeekState` is built by the test itself with a record `with` that replaces `Units` only, so that assertion pins **C# record-copy semantics**, not engine behaviour: deleting the line changes nothing. Mutation 3 confirms it — disabling the recompute fails at line 192 (tick 1), not at the mid-week clause.

DoD 3 is still literally satisfied and the PR body disclosed this honestly; the load-bearing halves (ticks 1 and 2) do go through the real coordinator. But the clause the test is named for is not the part doing the work.

### N4 — the starving tests pin the penalty *value*, not that it reduces `Moves`

Nothing in this file asserts that `ApplyTurn` actually subtracts the penalty. The reviewer's own mutation — `baseMoves - movesPenalty` → `baseMoves` — leaves **all nine tests green**.

DoD 2's "loses the extra move" is therefore met one step removed. It is not a repository-level hole (`ThraciaSupplyMoraleReplayTests` pins the behaviour), but one assertion through `ApplyTurn` — 50,000 troops / 10 tons → `Moves == BaseMoves(50_000) - 1` — would close it inside this file.

### N5 — a corpus id exists for a literal used here

`WeeklyMovesMaximumTests.cs:164` uses `48_173`, and `tests/fixtures/corpus.json` carries `roman13.troops = 48173` for that exact army. Merged precedent (`ArmyUpkeepTests.cs:32`, `ArmyPowerTests.cs:51`) names the id in a comment beside the literal. A nit; no fixture change is needed.

---

## Closed at merge, recorded for traceability

- **N3** — the PR body's DoD 4 claim that mutation 3 fails "only that test" is true of this file but not of the solution: it also fails the pre-existing `ThraciaSupplyMoraleReplayTests` and the CLI demo golden. The consequence is favourable (redundant coverage); only the wording overstated.

## Two observations reported separately by the reviewer

1. **`SupplyCapacity.PercentFull` overflows `int` above roughly 214,748 tons** (`supplyTons * 10000` in 32-bit), in merged T08 code. Unreachable at realistic supply levels — an army's capacity is `troops / 100` — so it is an observation rather than a defect worth its own bug. It is, however, exactly what makes N1 possible, so whoever fixes N1 should know it.
2. **`army-moves-field-signed-and-the-ffff-underflow.md` is not in `tests/fixtures/known-reports.json`** (manifest generated 2026-09-13). Nothing fails today, because no corpus entry cites that report — but the moment one does, T04's citation check fails. Per [build-process.md §2.4](https://github.com/diegoami/imperial_conquest_2/blob/main/docs/build-process.md) the top-up belongs to whichever task owns the mechanic; T45's entry explicitly forbade a fixture change, so it was correctly left. Worth doing with the next `tests/fixtures/**` change.

Blocks: T14, T16, T17

**Defect.** `src/IC2.Engine/Presentation/GameSession.cs:206` counts news-worthy events and `:230` then prints `State.NewsLog.Slots.TakeLast(newsAdded)`. That assumes **one news-log entry per news-worthy event**. T42 (`db5c231`) broke that assumption in two ways:
- `AppendRoundHeader` appends **2** entries (a blank line and the week header) backed by **no event at all**;
- a dash-wrapped `nation.conquered` appends **3** entries for **1** event.

**Effect.** A round-completing `end` that also produced one real news event prints only the week header and the blank line, and silently drops the news line. Verified in the code by T42's reviewer and independently by the main session.

**Why it's latent today.** The engine declares no news-worthy events yet, so nothing can hit it. It goes live in exactly the tasks T42 had to precede: T14 (fleet loss, storm damage), T16 (battles) and T17 (capture, the dash-wrapped conquest line).

**Evidence.** T42's review addendum: https://github.com/diegoami/imperial_conquest_2/pull/97#issuecomment-5722477051

**Why it wasn't reworked into T42.** The fix is in `src/IC2.Engine/Presentation/**`, outside T42's Owns list, and T42's own hazard forbids touching T41's code. Note the honest wrinkle the reviewer raised: T41's code was correct against T10's contract, and T42 changed that contract underneath it. T42's PR should have named `GameSession` as an affected consumer.

**Suggested fix.** The session should ask the log what it appended rather than infer it from the event count: either compare the log length before and after the turn, or have the writer return the entries it added. That is `src/IC2.Engine/Presentation/**`, which **T23** owns — but T23 comes after T17, so it can't be the fix. Needs a planner decision before T14/T16/T17 run: a small correction task, or an explicit widening of one of those tasks' Owns.
